items.attribution_note: Pakistan-nexus is the consensus of vendor reporting and MITRE ATT&CK. The tracker's confidence rates the evidence for the activity described here, not the attribution.
items.summary: A long-running espionage actor that primarily targets Indian government, defence and education sectors. Typical tradecraft is spear-phishing with weaponised documents and LNK files, and fake or trojanised apps, delivering RATs such as Crimson RAT, CapraRAT (Android) and Poseidon. 2026 reporting describes new RAT activity, LNK-based delivery chains, and expansion toward India's startup ecosystem.

attack.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic
Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder

key_findings: January 2026 campaigns sent a ZIP with an LNK disguised as a PDF; the LNK runs a remote HTA through mshta, which loads the RAT in memory and opens a decoy PDF.

February 2026: Acronis TRU attributed, with high confidence, a Crimson RAT campaign against Indian startups, particularly OSINT and cybersecurity firms, delivered as an ISO containing an LNK disguised as an Excel file.
Crimson RAT, a .NET RAT delivered through macro documents, remains the workhorse: file theft, screenshots, keylogging and command execution.
CapraRAT extends operations to Android through trojanised or fake apps.
Delivery has moved from macro documents to OLE and LNK-based chains, with repeated experiments targeting Linux desktops used in Indian government.

During the April-May 2025 India-Pakistan crisis, CloudSEK and Seqrite separated this group's phishing from the hacktivist noise: Pahalgam-themed .ppam, .xlam, .lnk and .msi lures, spoofed Indian defence domains, and Crimson RAT or Ares payloads aimed at government and defence users. CloudSEK rated it the more serious threat of the period.
recommended_actions: Disable Office macros by policy and treat .lnk files arriving by email or in archives as hostile.
Allow Play Store installs only on managed devices used by government and defence staff.
Hunt for Office spawning script interpreters or unknown .NET binaries, and new Run keys or scheduled tasks tied to document opens.
Use phishing-resistant MFA on government and defence mailboxes.

items.attribution_note: Linked to the Pakistan-nexus cluster through infrastructure and tooling overlap with Transparent Tribe; the group deliberately mimics SideWinder's TTPs to mislead attribution.
items.summary: A Pakistan-nexus espionage actor that mimics the SideWinder group's TTPs (hence the name) and is widely assessed to overlap with Transparent Tribe/APT36 infrastructure. It targets Indian government, defence and increasingly academic and research institutions. Typical delivery is a ZIP archive embedding an LNK or decoy document that leads to RATs such as ActionRAT, AllaKore and AuTo Stealer, hosted on compromised domains.
key_findings: The signature chain is a ZIP archive containing an LNK or decoy document that starts a multi-stage infection.
Next stages are usually pulled from compromised legitimate websites rather than attacker-registered infrastructure.
Payloads rotate between ActionRAT, AllaKore RAT, ReverseRAT and AuTo Stealer, which collects Office files, PDFs, databases and images.
Has exploited the WinRAR flaw CVE-2023-38831, where opening a decoy file inside a crafted archive runs the payload, and fielded a Linux variant of Ares RAT (Seqrite, Nov 2023).

The first public report (Seqrite, September 2020) already showed the hallmarks still seen today: LNK files with double extensions such as 'Defence-Production-Policy-2020.docx.lnk', HTA stages run through mshta, and DLL side-loading through a legitimate Windows binary.
recommended_actions: Block or quarantine .lnk files inside archives and alert on LNKs that spawn mshta, powershell or rundll32.
Keep WinRAR and other archive tools patched; SideCopy has exploited CVE-2023-38831.
Flag outbound connections from Office or Explorer to unusual websites right after a document opens.
Extend monitoring to research and academic units, which are now in scope.

It assesses a Pakistani origin, likely linked to Transparent Tribe.

items.attribution_note: Acronis attributes the June 2026 government and energy campaign to Mustang Panda with high confidence, citing code shared with the group's TONESHELL backdoor, command servers in a network block IBM X-Force tied to the group, and a reused side-loading chain. The April 2026 banking activity rests on shared code and infrastructure. MITRE ATT&CK describes Mustang Panda as a China-based espionage actor active since at least 2012.
items.summary: A China-based espionage group that turned on India in 2026. From March it sent Indian banks help-file attachments posing as HDFC Bank support tickets that installed the LOTUSLITE backdoor. In June it got into Indian government networks, including machines used by senior administrative staff, with lures about hydropower cooperation and an India-Taiwan memorandum of understanding, using Zoho WorkDrive as its command channel. Acronis, which reported both campaigns, worked with CERT-In on notification and clean-up.

attack.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Compiled HTML File
Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage

key_findings: Banking (Acronis, April 2026): a compiled help file, 'Request for Support.chm', bundles a legitimate executable, a rogue DLL and a page with a pop-up referencing HDFC Bank Limited. Clicking 'Yes' fetches JavaScript from cosmosmusic[.]com, which side-loads the updated LOTUSLITE (dnx.onecore.dll) through a Microsoft-signed binary. HDFC Bank is the impersonated brand, not a reported victim.

LOTUSLITE talks HTTPS to a dynamic-DNS server, editor.gleeze[.]com, and gives the operators a remote shell, file operations and session management. The new build changes the traffic 'magic value' from 0x8899AABB to 0xB2EBCFDF but keeps old internal names such as KugouMain and DataImporterMain.

The same build reached South Korean and US policy circles through a spoofed Gmail account impersonating Victor Cha and Google Drive links. Acronis had earlier tied LOTUSLITE to Venezuela-themed spear-phishing of US government targets in January 2026, at medium confidence.

Government and energy (Acronis, June 2026): two parallel campaigns used ZIP archives with hidden DLLs and lures about a hydropower cooperation proposal and an India-Taiwan institutional MoU. SHARDLOADER side-loads through signed Solid PDF Creator and Citrix Receiver binaries, then deploys MINIRECON, a reworked TONESHELL that beacons over WebSocket inside HTTPS, or ZOHOMURK.

ZOHOMURK carries hardcoded Zoho OAuth credentials and uses an attacker-owned WorkDrive account as a dead drop: it reads commands from one folder and writes stolen data to another, so its traffic looks like normal cloud use. Beacons were active from 12 to 22 June 2026.
Persistence was through Run keys and a scheduled task named SolidPDFPcl2Bmp, with a reported C2 domain couldinstallup[.]com. A recurring typo, 'RunOnece', appears across several implants.
recommended_actions: Block .chm attachments at the mail gateway, and alert when hh.exe starts a script host or makes a network connection.
Hunt for signed binaries running from ProgramData or user folders that load unsigned DLLs from the same folder, including Solid PDF Creator and Citrix Receiver components outside their install paths.
Zoho is widely used in India, so baseline first, then alert on Zoho WorkDrive API traffic or a 'Zoho Client/1.0' user agent from processes that are not a browser or an approved Zoho client.
Check endpoints for a scheduled task named SolidPDFPcl2Bmp and Run-key values containing 'RunOnece'.
Search DNS and proxy logs for editor.gleeze[.]com, cosmosmusic[.]com and couldinstallup[.]com (as reported, not re-validated).

items.attribution_note: Recorded Future assesses RedEcho as China-linked and notes overlaps with APT41 and Tonto Team infrastructure, but says the evidence is not enough to attribute it firmly to either; MITRE ATT&CK tracks it as G1042. TAG-38 is a different cluster that Recorded Future could not link to RedEcho; it is kept in this entry because it targeted the same assets. China denied both.
items.summary: China-nexus intrusions against India's power grid. Recorded Future disclosed RedEcho in February 2021 after it targeted ten Indian power-sector organisations, including four of the five Regional Load Despatch Centres, and two seaports with the ShadowPad backdoor. In April 2022 it reported a separate cluster, TAG-38, inside at least seven State Load Despatch Centres near Ladakh, using hacked DVR and IP cameras as command-and-control relays. Both periods followed India-China border tension.
key_findings: RedEcho (Recorded Future, February 2021): 21 IP addresses at ten Indian power generation and transmission organisations, including four of the five Regional Load Despatch Centres, a high-voltage substation and a coal-fired thermal plant, plus two seaports, communicated with ShadowPad infrastructure Recorded Future tracks as AXIOMATICASYMPTOTE.
The activity rose after the India-China border clashes of May 2020. Three of the targeted Indian IP addresses had been hit in a November 2020 APT41 campaign against Indian oil and gas organisations.

Maharashtra's cyber cell linked the October 2020 Mumbai blackout to malware at a State Load Despatch Centre. Recorded Future called the link to that outage unsubstantiated, so the tracker does not treat the outage as a confirmed cyber attack.

TAG-38 (Recorded Future, April 2022): at least seven State Load Despatch Centres near the Ladakh border, a national emergency response system and the Indian subsidiary of a multinational logistics company. ShadowPad was controlled through likely compromised internet-facing DVR and IP camera devices, with the open-source FastReverseProxy.
India's Power Minister said two attempts on load despatch centres near Ladakh were 'not successful'.
recommended_actions: Grid and OT operators: hunt for ShadowPad and PlugX on IT networks that touch SCADA, and confirm the IT/OT boundary blocks direct outbound connections.
Treat outbound traffic to consumer DVRs, IP cameras and routers as suspicious: TAG-38 used them as relays, so reputation-based blocking will not catch it.
Alert on FastReverseProxy (frp) binaries and long-lived reverse tunnels from servers.
Act on CERT-In and NCIIPC notifications as incidents, and keep logs long enough to scope activity that began months earlier.

items.attribution_note: The US, Japan and South Korea attribute the July 2024 WazirX theft to North Korea in a joint statement of 14 January 2025, which names the Lazarus Group among the DPRK actors the three countries have designated. The DTrack findings (Kaspersky) and the Cosmos Bank attribution (Securonix) come from vendors. Public reporting uses 'Lazarus' loosely for several DPRK clusters; MITRE ATT&CK tracks APT38 and Andariel separately.
items.summary: North Korea's state hacking apparatus, which steals money for the regime and spies for strategic intelligence. India has seen both sides. The DTrack spyware and its ATM-focused sibling ATMDtrack were found in Indian banks and research centres in 2018 and 2019, and DTrack was confirmed on the administrative network of the Kudankulam nuclear power plant in 2019. In July 2024, US$235 million was drained from the Indian exchange WazirX, a theft the US, Japan and South Korea attribute to North Korea.
key_findings: Kaspersky (September 2019): ATMDtrack, found in 2018, was built to get into Indian ATMs and steal card data. Code overlaps led to more than 180 samples of DTrack, a remote-access spy tool used against Indian financial institutions and research centres: keylogging, browser history, process and network listing, and file upload and download. It shares code with the 2013 DarkSeoul campaign attributed to Lazarus.
Kaspersky (October 2019) found DTrack samples across 18 Indian states, led by Maharashtra (24%), Karnataka (18.5%) and Telangana (12%).

Kudankulam: CERT-In notified NPCIL on 4 September 2019. After first denying any infection, NPCIL confirmed on 30 October that malware was found on the plant's administrative network, which it said is isolated from the plant systems. The malware was DTrack.

Cosmos Bank, Pune (10-13 August 2018): about Rs 94 crore stolen, roughly US$11.5 million through some 14,800 ATM withdrawals in 28 countries with cloned cards approved by a malicious proxy switch, plus about US$2 million in three SWIFT transfers to a Hong Kong account. Securonix attributed it to Lazarus; there is no government attribution.

WazirX (18 July 2024): about US$235 million was drained from a multisig wallet held with Liminal Custody after the attackers altered the wallet's controlling contract while signers approved transactions. WazirX and Liminal dispute where the compromise happened. Elliptic tied it to North Korea the same day.
WazirX resumed trading on 24 October 2025 under a Singapore court-sanctioned scheme that returned about 85% of users' balances.
recommended_actions: Banks, especially co-operative banks: reconcile ATM and card-switch authorisations against core banking in near real time, and alert when the switch approves transactions the core system never saw.
Keep SWIFT and payment-switch environments segmented from the corporate network with separate administrator credentials.
Crypto platforms: verify what a multisig transaction actually does on an independent device before signing; the WazirX signers approved altered transactions through the normal interface.
Critical infrastructure: treat a CERT-In notification as an incident, and keep administrative networks segmented from operational ones.
Hunt for DTrack behaviour: keyloggers writing to temporary files, collection of browser history, and command-line network and process discovery from unusual parents.

items.attribution_note: MITRE ATT&CK describes APT41 as a Chinese state-sponsored espionage group that also runs financially motivated operations. BlackBerry's 2021 attribution of the India-themed phishing rests on overlapping Cobalt Strike configurations and infrastructure.
items.summary: A prolific Chinese group that mixes espionage with crime. India appears in its reporting three times: among about 20 countries hit in a fast 2020 exploitation campaign against Citrix and Zoho ManageEngine; in a November 2020 campaign against Indian oil and gas organisations; and in 2021 phishing aimed at Indian nationals with fake tax and COVID-19 notices. There has been no India-specific public reporting since 2021, but the group remains active worldwide.
key_findings: FireEye (March 2020): between 20 January and 11 March 2020, APT41 exploited Citrix ADC and Gateway (CVE-2019-19781) and Zoho ManageEngine Desktop Central (CVE-2020-10189) at organisations in about 20 countries, India among them.
Recorded Future noted a November 2020 APT41 campaign against Indian oil and gas organisations, three of whose IP addresses later appeared in RedEcho's targeting.

BlackBerry (October 2021): three phishing schemes aimed at Indian nationals, with PDFs posing as government tax and COVID-19 notices. Payloads arrived as embedded PowerShell, a self-extracting archive or a ZIP, and loaded Cobalt Strike Beacon with a custom malleable C2 profile and lookalike Microsoft domains.
recommended_actions: Patch internet-facing appliances and management servers within days of a KEV listing: APT41 exploited both 2020 flaws within weeks of disclosure.
Treat PDFs claiming to be tax or health notices from the government as high-risk when they arrive by email with an archive or script.
Detect Cobalt Strike on the network (beacon timing, malleable profiles) and on hosts (named pipes, injected rundll32), and monitor for lookalike Microsoft domains.

items.attribution_note: Recorded Future linked RedFoxtrot to PLA Unit 69010 in Urumqi, Xinjiang, after one operator's lax operational security exposed his location, his interest in hacking and a suspected past affiliation with the PLA's former Communications Command Academy in Wuhan. This is single-vendor attribution.
items.summary: A Chinese military-linked espionage group that Recorded Future tracked back to 2014 across India and Central Asia. In the six months before its June 2021 report, the focus was India: multiple aerospace and defence contractors and telecommunications companies. Its toolkit (ShadowPad, PlugX, Poison Ivy, IceFog, PCShare and the Royal Road document builder) is shared across Chinese groups. There has been no public reporting on it since 2021.
key_findings: Recorded Future (16 June 2021) tracked RedFoxtrot activity back to 2014 against targets in India, Afghanistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan.
In the six months before the report, it focused on India: multiple aerospace and defence contractors, and telecommunications companies.

Tools: IceFog, ShadowPad, Royal Road, PCShare, PlugX and Poison Ivy, plus web servers used to host payloads and collect stolen data. Royal Road builds documents that exploit old Microsoft Office flaws.
Attribution came from the operator's online footprint, not from the malware, which is shared widely among Chinese groups.
recommended_actions: Defence, aerospace and telecom firms: hunt for ShadowPad and PlugX loaders, which are shared across several China-nexus groups, so a hit warrants a full investigation whichever group it belongs to.
Patch or remove the old Office Equation Editor and block RTF attachments from outside the organisation where possible.
Keep historical logs: this group's activity was disclosed years after it began.

items.attribution_note: US Cyber Command (January 2022) and a joint US/UK advisory (February 2022) describe MuddyWater as a subordinate element of Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS); MITRE ATT&CK and vendor reporting agree. The tracker's confidence rates the evidence for activity against India, not the attribution.
items.summary: A long-running Iranian espionage actor whose main focus is the Middle East, with India named repeatedly among its secondary targets: in its first documented campaigns in 2017, and in a 2023–2024 campaign that sent small businesses in India phishing links to legitimate remote-access software. It is still active in 2026, and DSCI's March 2026 advisory lists it among the Iranian state actors Indian organisations should watch after the Iran war began. No India-specific campaign has been publicly reported; India appears in multi-country target lists.

attack.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic
OS Credential Dumping: Security Account Manager
Credentials from Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers

key_findings: Palo Alto Unit 42's first public report on the group (November 2017) lists India among the countries targeted or suspected to be targeted from February to October 2017, alongside Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Israel, the UAE, Georgia, Pakistan, Turkey and the US. Delivery was macro-enabled Word documents dropping the POWERSTATS PowerShell backdoor.

HarfangLab (April 2024) documented an October 2023 to April 2024 campaign against small businesses in Israel, India, Algeria, Turkey, Italy and Egypt, across sectors including airlines, IT, telecommunications, pharmaceuticals, logistics and travel. Spear-phishing emails linked to free file-hosting services (Egnyte, Onehub, filetransfer.io) that served the legitimate Atera Agent remote-management tool.

The Atera agents were registered with compromised business and personal email accounts, and in one case lures were sent from a victim's own compromised mailbox to its contacts. Using signed, legitimate remote-management software gives the group a foothold that most antivirus will not flag.

In 2025, Group-IB reported a campaign against more than 100 government entities in the Middle East and North Africa using a compromised mailbox, macro documents and the Phoenix backdoor. India was not named.

In 2026, Symantec and Carbon Black reported intrusions at nine organisations in nine countries using DLL side-loading through legitimately signed binaries, a Node.js implant chain, browser credential theft (ChromElevator), SAM hive theft and SOCKS5 tunnelling. The named victim was in South Korea; India was not named.

DSCI's March 2026 advisory on the Middle East conflict lists MuddyWater, with APT33, APT34, Handala and CyberAv3ngers, among the Iranian actors posing risk to Indian organisations, especially IT/ITeS firms with Gulf, Israeli or Western clients. It does not report a specific MuddyWater intrusion in India.
recommended_actions: Inventory and allowlist remote-management tools; alert on any unapproved Atera, ScreenConnect, SimpleHelp, Syncro or RemoteUtilities install.
Treat links to free file-hosting services in unsolicited email as high risk, including mail from known partners whose accounts may be compromised.
Block Office macros in files from the internet.
Hunt for signed executables loading DLLs from user-writable paths, node.exe or Office spawning PowerShell, and outbound SOCKS tunnels from workstations.
IT/ITeS providers with Middle Eastern clients: apply the same scrutiny to client-facing accounts and shared tooling, since supply-chain access is the main route DSCI expects.

items.summary: Regional context: one of South Asia's most active APTs, assessed as India-nexus, historically targeting Pakistan, Nepal, China and Afghanistan and more recently expanding to maritime, nuclear and IT sectors across Asia, the Middle East and Africa. Primarily spear-phishing with weaponised documents exploiting known Office flaws. Included here for regional awareness; its targets are largely outside India.
key_findings: Kaspersky's March 2025 research: a DOCX uses remote template injection to fetch an RTF that exploits CVE-2017-11882 and delivers Backdoor Loader and StealerBot.
Primarily spear-phishing with weaponised documents that exploit known Office flaws.
Has expanded from Pakistan, Nepal, China and Afghanistan to maritime, nuclear and IT sectors across Asia, the Middle East and Africa.
recommended_actions: Patch Office promptly; SideWinder relies on known, already-fixed document exploits.
